plannedScenes.narrationText: Deep inside an unmarked concrete facility in Northern Virginia, thirty thousand processors hum in unison. They are generating answers, code, synthetic voices, and digital illusions for hundreds of millions of people across the globe.

sequenceParams.title: The AI Gold Rush
sequenceParams.subtitle: Who controls the world's computing power?

plannedScenes.narrationText: When ChatGPT launched in late 2022, it crossed one hundred million monthly active users in just sixty days. By comparison, it took Instagram two and a half years, and Spotify more than three years to reach that same threshold. The world had never adopted a technology this quickly.

sequenceParams.consequence: A *hundred million* people found the machine before the machine found a home.

plannedScenes.narrationText: To understand where this power comes from, follow a single prompt. When you ask an artificial intelligence a question, your request travels through high-speed fiber into a specialized cluster of GPUs arranged in monolithic server racks.

Each modern AI server rack draws over forty kilowatts of electricity. Eight specialized graphics processors work in parallel, pushing data across copper and optical interconnects. Air cooling is no longer enough; liquid must circulate directly over the silicon die.

Building and operating this physical footprint requires capital on a scale few entities on Earth can assemble. Today, three corporate giants—Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud—control roughly sixty-five percent of the entire global cloud infrastructure.

sequenceParams.consequence: Three companies *decide* where the intelligence lives.

plannedScenes.narrationText: Every token generated has an ecological weight. A single complex query to a frontier large language model consumes approximately 3.2 watt-hours of electrical energy—more than ten times the power of a standard search engine query.

sequenceParams.consequence: A single answer costs *ten times* a search.

plannedScenes.narrationText: Every answer has a cost. Every model has a home. Neither is neutral.

sequenceParams.text: Every answer has a cost. Every model has a home. *Neither is neutral*.
